A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same representation-hierarchy study of pruning. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable matching despite reordered appendices and redesigned figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning benchmark evaluations, representation measurements, approximation-validation experiments, and temperature sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports empirical representation analyses, including revised diagnostic trajectories and the retained appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The pruning procedures and representation-hierarchy framework remain the same. Section 5 more explicitly describes the existing single-layer intervention under the baseline model's context, without establishing a changed algorithm, architecture, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The displayed benchmark coverage and Table 3 prompts remain unchanged. New Appendix A lists ARC-Challenge without corresponding results and identifies C4 calibration data. The PDFs do not establish whether these represent expanded data use or newly disclosed details of existing experiments.

E2.justification: Wanda, SparseGPT, Attention/MLP Drop, ShortGPT, and AWQ already participate in v1's comparisons. SparseGPT moves from Figure 10 to Figure 9, and the AWQ comparison moves from Figure 9 to Figure 12; neither is newly evaluated in v3.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 changes the reported attention layer for the representative Figure 6 validation from the 12th to the 14th. Newly specified calibration, sparsity, and MBPP settings are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish that those settings changed or that benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 revises the evidence examining layerwise pruning sensitivity and approximation accuracy in Figures 6 and 13–18. The same temperature ablation, pruning-versus-quantization comparison, and generation-failure case study remain, without a new class of robustness tests or ablated components.

E5.justification: Figure 7 acquires shaded bands absent from v1, but their meaning and computation are unspecified. Whether these constitute statistical uncertainty reporting or another plotting treatment cannot be determined. Figure 4's existing mean and min–max reporting remains, with no newly stated replication or seed counts.

E6.justification: V3 substantially replaces the quantitative representation-analysis evidence: Figures 14–18 show different layerwise KL, angular-deviation, and relative-magnitude trajectories, alongside changed Figures 5–6 and 13. These are revised diagnostic results, not demonstrated performance gains. Table 1's numerical results and Table 2's generated examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The three approximations and autoregressive error decomposition remain. Local corrections fix Theorem 1's orthogonal-component definition and replace the variance characterization in v1 Appendix C.1 with orthogonal magnitude in v3 Appendix D.1. Theorem 2's discussion also correctly identifies the relevant perturbation as delta z rather than z.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claim that the LM head further attenuates deviations and produces higher similarity to preserving comparable similarity. The main claims about task-dependent pruning robustness, softmax amplification, and categorical-token subspace stability remain.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 and the supplementary discussion soften the interpretation of reduced orthogonal energy: it is now consistent with limited logit perturbations rather than establishing inherent attenuation by the linear projection. The autoregressive-feedback explanation and training-free-pruning limitation remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix A specifies 128 randomly sampled C4 calibration sequences, 50% sparsity for intra-layer experiments, and 3-shot MBPP evaluation. Section 5 clarifies the shared baseline context for layerwise interventions. These are useful disclosures; both PDFs retain the same repository link.

R1.justification: V3 adds Raffel et al. for C4 and Thakur et al. for BEIR, and removes the Langley reference. The related-work argument and positioning remain substantially unchanged; shortened author lists and completed bibliographic metadata do not introduce additional research relationships.

P1.justification: V3 cleans up grammar and terminology, expands the intervention explanation, introduces an implementation-details appendix, and moves quantization discussion from Appendix F to I. The main section sequence and most of the narrative remain intact, while long bibliographic author lists are abbreviated.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively redrawn with revised sizing, typography, ticks, legends, and shared axis labels. Figure 2 is rearranged, Table 2 and several main-text figures move, and Figure 7 gains shading. This is substantial visual reworking, although v3 introduces clipped legends in Figure 11.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reproducibility through the calibration and evaluation disclosures and clearer intervention description. Local mathematical corrections and the narrower LM-head claim improve precision. These benefits outweigh localized presentation problems, including undefined Figure 7 bands and clipped Figure 11 legends, while the main benchmark evidence and theoretical framework remain largely unchanged.
